flags.headline: STLD -2.96% — continued decline on Q2 guidance cut (aluminum write-down), matches flagged earnings-cyclicality risk
flags.detail: Steel Dynamics fell 2.96% today, part of a continuing pullback (down ~14.75% over recent weeks per secondary reporting) following its Q2 2026 EPS guidance cut to $3.51-$3.55, which included a $16M write-down tied to a Mississippi aluminum-facility relocation. No new news specific to today's session was found; this is continued drift on the guidance-cut event rather than a fresh shock. Analyst price targets have been raised in places ($255.91→$272.09) even as the stock has fallen, reflecting a split between near-term earnings disappointment and longer-term steel-pricing optimism.
flags.thesis_link: Matches STLD key_risk: 'Steel price cyclicality — profit margin of 7.22% is thin and earnings can swing 20%+ year-to-year with steel price cycles, as demonstrated by the FY2024-to-FY2025 earnings decline despite record volumes.' A guidance cut driven by an unplanned write-down is a direct instance of that earnings-swing risk. Severity escalated one tier (would otherwise be AMBER) per thesis-match rule.

flags.headline: AEM +2.89% today (technical bounce) — persisting RED, Barnat impact now quantified: 60-80k oz lost 2H2026 production, formal update due 7/29
flags.detail: AEM rose 2.89% today but the underlying thesis risk is unresolved and better quantified since last run: the July 1 Barnat pit wall-movement incident (Canadian Malartic complex) is now expected to reduce H2 2026 production by 60,000-80,000 oz of gold, with full-year 2026 guidance likely landing near the low end of the prior 3.3-3.5Moz range, and up to ~150k oz/year of reduced 2027-2028 production. No injuries, equipment damage, or environmental impact reported. Formal updated guidance is confirmed still due with Q2 results on 2026-07-29. Held at RED on the unresolved catalyst, not on today's price move.
flags.thesis_link: Matches AEM key_risk on valuation sensitivity to production/growth execution — a confirmed multi-year production cut is a direct materialization of that risk, now with hard numbers attached.

flags.headline: Strait of Hormuz shipping 'ground to a halt' amid renewed US-Iran fighting — oil elevated, cross-sleeve watch item
flags.detail: Traceable tanker crossings via the US-coordinated Strait of Hormuz route have effectively stopped since July 7 amid resumed US-Iran fighting; the US also revoked an Iran oil-sale authorization. Brent crude is up ~$4/bbl week-over-week (~$76.58 as of Friday), with analysts flagging $10-15 further upside risk if disruption persists, particularly for diesel given lost Middle East and Russian refining capacity. Equity markets have so far taken this in stride (SPY +0.84%, QQQ +1.66% today) rather than pricing in full-blown conflict risk. No single held name has a confirmed name-specific catalyst from this yet, but it is a live risk to the energy sleeve (DVN, VLO, OKE, CVX, CNX) in both directions — higher crude helps E&P/midstream economics but a genuine supply shock or extended closure would be broadly risk-off.
